The correct maximum is 4 choose 2 pairs × 2 points each = 12 distinct intersection points, since each pair of circles meets in at most 2 points and the points can all be distinct (circles in general position).

The proposed solution gets 14, which exceeds this bound. Its counting is also flawed: it has circles 3 and 4 passing through A and B, so those points are shared rather than new, and it claims 4 new points for the third circle and 8 for the fourth, which would require more than 2 points per pair. The answer 14 is wrong.
